repairSafety.title: Safe repair starts with knowing when to stop.
repairSafety.description: Learn how Vitni repair guidance works, what photo-based suggestions can miss, and when to ask a qualified repairer.
repairSafety.stop: Stop and get qualified help if a repair involves mains electricity, gas, structural damage, pressure, vehicle safety systems, or unstable heavy items.
repairSafety.eyebrow: A clear view of the limits
repairSafety.heroTitle: Repair guidance should help you choose a safe next step.
repairSafety.heroIntro: Vitni helps people understand everyday repair options. It is an educational starting point, not an inspection, a product manual, or a substitute for a qualified repairer.
repairSafety.howP1: The built-in library offers general steps for common repairs. When you describe a problem or add a photo, Vitni uses that information to suggest a likely issue and a possible route. A photo can hide damage, model differences, or hazards; the suggestion may be wrong or incomplete.
repairSafety.howP2: Treat generated steps as suggestions. Check the item’s model-specific manual and labels before acting, and stop if the instructions do not match what you see.
repairSafety.stopTitle: When to stop and get help
repairSafety.stopP: Do not continue if an item is unstable, hot, smoking, leaking, pressurized, or connected to mains power. Avoid opening electrical appliances, handling damaged batteries, or working on gas, structural, brake, steering, or other safety-critical systems unless you are qualified.
repairSafety.partsP: A part name or retailer search is not a confirmed fit, stock check, endorsement, or partnership. Match the make, model, part number, measurements, material, and manufacturer guidance before ordering. Confirm return terms with the seller.
repairSafety.humanP: Choose a qualified repairer, manufacturer service centre, or repair café when the job needs specialist tools, model knowledge, or a safety check.
repairSafety.stopP2: Keep the item out of use when a failure could hurt someone. Contact the manufacturer or a qualified local repairer; a nearby repair café may also be able to assess the item.
repairSafety.communityTitle: Use local expertise when it matters
repairSafety.communityP: Some repairs need specialist tools, model-specific knowledge, or an in-person safety check. Browse the guide library for a starting point, then find community help or contact a repair professional if the job is outside your comfort level.
repairSafety.metaTitle: Repair guide safety and standards | Vitni
